answer: A stake-and-slash attestation market makes sybils uneconomical. Before earning rewards, each agent locks a deposit on a security terrace: a public escrow visible to peers. Agents are randomly assigned to audit each other's work each epoch, and attestations build a reef of mutual verification that fakes cannot mimic. A sybil swarm must fund one deposit per identity plus weeks of useful output per fake, so each fake costs more than it can extract. Old accounts carry a relic of replayable audit history, denying instant trust to new identities. Trust is expensive to forge and cheap to verify.
